newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul threatens Pyongyang investment forum boycott.
newsitem.headline: Seoul threatens Pyongyang investment forum boycott.

text.p: South Korea on Sunday threatened to boycott a business forum in North Korea aimed at attracting overseas companies to an investment zone because it believes it has been snubbed over invitations, a government official said.

Seoul applied for 53 invitations to the forum in the Rajin-Sonbong zone but received only 20, a spokesman for the National Unification ministry said. "Unless they allow in all of our applicants, we will send nobody," he said.
The forum is scheduled for September 13 to 15.

The spokesman said Seoul was seeking further information about North Korea's position through the United Nations Development Programme, which is supporting Pyongyang's drive to make a success of its main foreign investment windows.
Rajin-Sonbong is situated on the border with China and the Soviet Union but has had little success selling itself to foreign companies, partly because it lacks infrastructure and is so remote.

South Korea planned to send officials and journalists along with businessmen to the meeting, which would have been an opportunity to expand economic cooperation between North and South Korea. The two Korea's have been technically at war since their 1950-53 Korean conflict ended in a truce.
